artists.biography: Jesus Jones are a British alternative dance band. The Wiltshire-based group, formed in late 1988, recorded and performed in the late 1980s, throughout the 1990s, and into the 2000s. They are best remembered for their track, "Right Here, Right Now", an international hit and subsequently globally appropriated for promotional and advertising campaigns. They are also well-remembered for the songs "Real Real Real" and "International Bright Young Thing."

perplexity.description:
Liquidizer, released in 1989 on Food Records (not Speedowax Records), is the debut album by British rock band Jesus Jones. Musically, the album is a high-energy fusion of dance-rock, alternative rock, and electronic elements, characterized by relentless tempos, prominent synth lines, driving dance beats, and layers of samples including sirens, telephones, and vocal snippets. The album’s sound is dense and futuristic for its time, blending grinding guitar melodies with breakbeats and pop hooks, creating what critics have described as a “blistering” and “unrelenting freak out” that stands out for its originality and intensity. Tracks like “Info Freako,” “Bring It On Down,” and “Never Enough” exemplify the band’s knack for short, sharp, and impactful songs that never lose momentum.

Within Jesus Jones’ discography, Liquidizer is regarded as their most distinctive and groundbreaking work, establishing their signature style before their later commercial breakthrough with Doubt. While subsequent albums leaned more toward mainstream accessibility, Liquidizer remains celebrated for its raw energy, innovative use of technology, and its role in pioneering the dance-rock crossover in the UK. Critics have noted its historical significance, with many considering it the band’s definitive album and a cult classic of the era. Upon its original release, Liquidizer reached number 31 on the UK Albums Chart and earned praise for its originality, though it was later overshadowed commercially by the band’s follow-up. Its reputation has endured, with retrospective reviews highlighting its influence and unique sonic identity.
